hints: Focus on the two clues separately, the colour of the silver halide precipitate and what happens in concentrated ammonia.
Recall that $\text{AgCl}$ is white, $\text{AgBr}$ is cream to pale yellow, and $\text{AgI}$ is yellow, with very different solubility in ammonia.
Think about what mixture would look pale yellow at first, then lose its lighter part in concentrated ammonia to leave a darker yellow solid behind.
walkthrough:
**Recall the silver halide colours**

Silver chloride is white, silver bromide is cream or pale yellow, and silver iodide is yellow to darker yellow.

Precipitation reaction:
$$\text{Ag}^{+}(aq) + \text{X}^{-}(aq) \rightarrow \text{AgX}(s)$$

**Recall solubility in ammonia**

$\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia. $\text{AgBr}$ dissolves only in concentrated aqueous ammonia. $\text{AgI}$ does not dissolve even in concentrated aqueous ammonia.

**Interpret the first observation**

A pale yellow precipitate suggests more than one colour mixed together. A white solid mixed with a yellow solid can appear pale yellow overall.

**Interpret the second observation**

Partly dissolving in concentrated ammonia means one part is soluble ($\text{AgCl}$ or $\text{AgBr}$) and one part is insoluble ($\text{AgI}$). Leaving a darker yellow precipitate tells us the insoluble residue is $\text{AgI}$.

So the original powder must have supplied $\text{I}^{-}$ plus another halide that gives a soluble silver salt, and the pale colour points to white $\text{AgCl}$ mixing with yellow $\text{AgI}$.

options.A: Sodium bromide only would give cream or pale yellow $\text{AgBr}$. This would dissolve completely in concentrated ammonia, so nothing would be left. It cannot leave a darker yellow residue.
options.B: Sodium iodide only would give yellow $\text{AgI}$. This is insoluble even in concentrated ammonia, so the precipitate would not partly dissolve at all.
options.C: A mixture of chloride and bromide would give $\text{AgCl}$ and $\text{AgBr}$. Both dissolve in concentrated ammonia ($\text{AgCl}$ even in dilute), so the precipitate would dissolve completely with no darker yellow solid remaining.
options.D: A mixture of chloride and iodide gives white $\text{AgCl}$ and yellow $\text{AgI}$ together, which looks pale yellow. In concentrated ammonia the $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves away, leaving insoluble darker yellow $\text{AgI}$. This matches both observations perfectly.
